name: Sending a global payout with nothing but an email
object: Stripe's global payouts, sending money to any recipient worldwide by email from the Balances dashboard, one at a time or in bulk by CSV
audience: finance and operations teams at platforms who pay out to contractors, vendors, or customers internationally
message: This video tells platform operators that Stripe can send money to anyone in the world with nothing but an email address, one at a time or by the hundreds.

moments.what: a presenter stands in front of the Balances dashboard on the Stripe Sessions stage and explains that paying someone normally means collecting and storing their bank details by hand
moments.copy: Normally paying someone involves collecting and storing their bank account details, which is manual and prone to error.

moments.what: clicks Send from the top bar, enters only a recipient's email address, adds an amount and a memo, and sends a one-time payout live on screen
moments.copy: I'm also able to send a one-time payout to basically anyone in the world with just an email.

moments.what: shows the email the recipient receives, and notes that a recipient who already has Link saved can claim the funds in a few clicks
moments.copy: Your recipient will get an email that looks like this, and if they already have their bank details stored with Link, they can receive money in just a few clicks.

moments.what: switches to bulk mode, uploads a CSV of recipients; the dashboard parses the total amount and every recipient's email, with an option to schedule the send for later
moments.copy: If you wanted to send payouts to a larger group of people, you can simply upload a CSV with all the details.

cta: no spoken call to action; the feature demo itself, from one recipient to a bulk CSV, is staged as the pitch
why: Showing the same mental model scale from a single email-only payout to a bulk CSV send in one unbroken take proves the feature works at both ends of a platform's payout volume without the viewer having to imagine it.
